```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(1)
```


# Problem 1

I wrote a function to simulate birthdays for a group of people and check whether at least two people share the same birthday. Each birthday is randomly sampled from 365 possible days with replacement. The function returns TRUE if there is a shared birthday and FALSE otherwise.


```{r birthday-function}
birthday_match = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, group_size, replace = TRUE)
  n_distinct(birthdays) < group_size
}
```

## Running the simulations

I ran the function 10,000 times for each group size from 2 to 50 and recorded whether a shared birthday occurred in each simulation.

```{r birthday-simulations}
birthday_sim_df = 
  expand_grid( group_size = 2:50, iteration = 1:10000 ) |>
  mutate( shared_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_match) )
```


## Estimating the probabilities

For each group size, I estimated the probability of a shared birthday by taking the mean of the simulation results. Since TRUE is treated as 1 and FALSE as 0, the mean gives the proportion of simulations with a shared birthday.

```{r birthday-summary}
birthday_prob_df = 
  birthday_sim_df |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize( probability = mean(shared_birthday) )

birthday_prob_df |>
  filter(group_size %in% c(2, 10, 23, 30, 40, 50)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Plotting the probabilities

The following plot shows how the estimated probability of a shared birthday changes with group size.

```{r birthday-plot}
birthday_prob_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) + labs( title = "Probability of a Shared Birthday by Group Size", x = "Group size", y = "Estimated probability" ) +
  scale_x_continuous( breaks = c(2, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50) ) + 
  scale_y_continuous( breaks = c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1), limits = c(0, 1) )
```

## Results

The estimated probability of a shared birthday increases as the group size grows. For a group of 23 people, the estimated probability is `r round(100 * birthday_prob_df$probability[birthday_prob_df$group_size == 23], 1)`%, while for a group of 50 people, it increases to `r round(100 * birthday_prob_df$probability[birthday_prob_df$group_size == 50], 1)`%. The probability reaches approximately 50% with only 23 people, which is surprising given that there are 365 possible birthdays.


# Problem 2

## Importing the data

I first listed all the participant files and used `map()` to read each file into a list column.

```{r import, message=FALSE}
participant_files_df =
  tibble( file_name = list.files("./data", pattern = "^con_|^exp_") ) |>
  mutate( subject_data = purrr::map( file_name, \(file) read_csv(str_c("./data/", file)) ) )
```
